title: Johnny Hodges' death and his relationship with Duke
summary: Hodges' death in 1970 was a blow; Cootie says he and Duke were very close.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, now, in '70 was another tour of the Far East. And '70, I guess, was the first real bad blow for the band, when Johnny died.
Yeah. A real bad blow.
I guess nothing was ever really quite the
same after that, was it? I mean, you know, it couldn't be quite the same after that.
No.

There's something I want to ask you about that, if -- I don't know whether you want to say or not, but Duke and Johnny had such a funny relationship. Of course I realize that for any band leader, he's always scared to death of his stars, because everything is working so that they're always going to hit them for something more. And you know, as an ex-bandleader, that there isn't all that money like guys in the band think there is. A bandleader has a lot of problems, and a lot of financial problems, right?
That's right.

And he is always scared, because a thing mushrooms and grows, and every time you have to say yes, you're scared the next time is coming up again. Right? Don't you think, in a way, that had to influence Duke's relationship with Johnny, because Johnny was one of his most important voices.
I don't think so.
Don't you?
That was a very close relationship there, between those two. Always, you know. Johnny was real close to him, you know. They was real tight.
Oh. I'm so glad to hear you say that,
because you know what a funny guy Johnny was about all -- you know how deadpan he was, and all those funny things he would say up on the stand.
It didn't mean nothing.
It didn't mean nothing. No. It was really funny, wasn't it?
Yeah.
I mean, it was Johnny's humor, wasn't it?
Yeah. (Unintelligible) -- came down to Duke, himself.

But there was one thing, though, Cootie, I mean, that is that, of course, he used to have had to keep Johnny's things toward the end, like he did yours too. But nobody ever got to hear enough of Johnny. I mean, you never got to get that one last more encore that you wanted. And don't you think that maybe Duke had to do it that way --
He played enough.
(Laughter)
